Definition: a dove (apparently from the warmth of their mating)
BiblicalUsage: Yonah is the dove, and it appears at the turning points of the story. In Genesis 8:8 Noah sends forth a dove "to see if the waters were abated from off the face of the ground," and the bird comes back with the sign that the flood is ending. Leviticus 1:14 makes turtledoves and young pigeons the burnt offering of the poor, and Numbers 6:10 brings two of them to the priest at the end of a vow. Even in famine the dove is reckoned valuable, as 2 Kings 6:25 shows in besieged Samaria.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the dove is the Bible's picture of gentleness carrying good news. I hold that God chose a small, plain bird to tell Noah the waters were going down, and chose the same bird as the offering a poor person could bring, which tells me he notices the small and the poor. My position is that yonah teaches me to look for God's mercy in quiet, ordinary signs.
